analysis: Documentation-only changes. docs/architecture/inference.md: the changed ranges (head 3, 810-813, 829) document that GLM5Next video decoding now accepts variable-frame-rate MP4/QuickTime tracks. Frames are indexed at i/nominalFrameRate, in presentation order, instead of VFR being refused. The doc states that the existing bounds still apply: the 512 MiB maximumDecodedBytes decoded-frame cap, the 28,532 visual-token prepared-pixel cap and the videoTokenCeiling/mediaReservation budget. It also states that media remains excluded from prefix lookup/capture (permitsHybridCheckpoint), so T-041 is unaffected. The supplied head_text units 14/15 (lines 2036-2599) are unchanged context covering MiMo, Flint, Qwen4 and Bonsai. docs/provider/cli-reference.md line 52 mirrors the VFR note, and line 3 is a date bump. No security control, encryption, attestation, authorization or cache policy is changed in these docs. Integration question: the actual GLM5NextProcessor.decodeAsset source change was not supplied. A follow-up should confirm three points. First, VFR acceptance keeps the decoded-frame/token caps enforced before allocation. Second, a malicious consumer (ADV-002) cannot use a crafted VFR track, for example a tiny or zero nominalFrameRate or extreme frame counts, to cause unbounded iteration or a mismatched 2 FPS sampling that exhausts memory (TB-007 availability). Third, a nominalFrameRate of zero or NaN is refused rather than dividing by zero. This is not evidenced as a regression here.
